messages.author: 990bd78abe1370d4
messages.subject: update on progress
parts:
Hi!

 

The first sprint of our project to refactor the gbm package ended a few days ago and we’ve submitted an enormous pull request against gbm-developers/gbm.  Because of the structure of the code we have had to touch an awful lot of it, at once, to make any changes, and we expect the size of patches to decrease over time!  We largely spent this sprint refactoring the use of the adMisc parameter and changing the initialization of the distribution classes.  Towards the end of the sprint we did some initial refactoring of the data object, and this led to a reduction in several function signatures within the C++ code.

 

The current sprint will finish the refactoring of this data object by:


- storing the distribution with the data,
- and refactoring the GBM object so that it stores the opaque data.

 

This should lead to a further reduction in function signatures.

 

In the second half of this sprint we’ll review the structure of the tree objects and fitting.  This review will propose a design which should reduce the function signatures in the code and, again, improve maintainability via abstraction.  The output from this review will form the primary goal of the subsequent sprint where the tree class, and its associated classes, will be refactored.  Once we’ve got all this stable we’re looking to move on to coxph.

 

Again we hope to have all of these changes merged into the gbm-developers/gbm in two weeks or so.  We welcome any/all feedback or suggestions; to view the progress look at https://github.com/scientific-computing-solutions/gbm.

 

We’ve got a couple of requests.


1. Anyone who can think of good tests that we can apply to this package – please get in touch!

2.  Can those who have push access to gbm-developers/gbm please be a bit careful?  Ideally it would help if you can submit pull requests rather than pushing things directly to the repo.

--
pdm

messages.author: c2082155b3674058
messages.subject: Re: update on progress
parts:
Paul,
   I'll send an update of my Cox model code sometime in the next week.  It's in response to a very nasty data set someone sent me, which manages to cause a case weight exp(X beta) of about 2e+65.  I've changed the order of operations inside one loop to avoid doing a subtraction (small change) but haven't run all the tests yet.  Because it's not doing linear extrapolation GBM would, I think, never toss such a bizzare predictor at my subroutine so the change may not really be necessary; but all of the survival and coxme code is getting it.  (Because of the near infinite case weight the result of the subtraction had 0 digits of accuracy.)
  It sounds like I'll be ahead of your changes.  I appreciate the work that you are doing. 
Terry T.
